infra.text: How this Mac is set up, how to check it, and how to get it back when something breaks.
The watchdog reads every service's health every 30 seconds and shows it on System.
The heartbeat pings Healthchecks.io every 5 minutes; a missed ping emails you.
The restore drill runs on the first Sunday of each month and must pass.
After a power cut the Mac waits at the FileVault unlock screen. Unlock it, then wait for the working drive to mount before Brain shows all clear.
Brain is reachable only over Tailscale. The Mac's own key never expires; your phone's key is renewed while the internet is up.

run-0004.text: What to do when the working drive does not mount after a restart.
Check the cable and that the drive's light is on.
Open Disk Utility and unlock the drive with the key from the keychain.
If it still won't mount, Brain keeps running on the internal SSD and says so.

adr-0007.text: We run local models through MLX because it is the fastest free runtime on Apple silicon.
Models are converted once and checksummed in quarantine.
A model that has no MLX build waits until one exists.

prd-0003.text: Lease Reminders tells each tenant, by text, a set number of days before rent and lease dates, with the wording you approved.
A reminder to a new tenant waits for your approval the first time.

des-0009.text: Reminders are scheduled by the pipeline engine, not by cron, so pausing work pauses them.
The conformance record shows each requirement of PRD-0003 with the test that covers it.

rs-readme.text: Receipt Scanner reads photos of receipts and files the totals under Finance.
The Saturday audit found that this README still names the old inbox folder.

run-restore.text: How to bring back one record from the backups without touching the rest.
Pick the record and the point in time.
The record appears in a side folder; nothing is overwritten.

/: Today shows whether everything is all right and what needs you. Tiles are colored by status, and anything waiting on you is under Needs you.
/spend: Everything is free by default. A paid feature only costs money once you turn it on, and spending stops at its monthly cap.
/backups: You are on the starter backup: the two drives back each other up. It does not survive theft or fire until a backup drive is connected.
/approvals: An approval waits for you and never approves on timeout. If it lapses, nothing is sent.
/docs: Docs are the platform's own documentation. Open one to read it, ask me about it, or request a change, which becomes a work item.

quick_cards.title: Get help now
steps: Call emergency services. If there is no signal, send someone for help.
Stay with the person and keep them still and warm.
Note the time and what happened, for the responders.
quick_cards.source: American Red Cross First Aid manual

quick_cards.title: Severe bleeding
steps: Call emergency services if you can.
Press firmly on the wound with a clean cloth and keep pressing.
If blood soaks through, add more cloth on top. Do not lift the first one.
quick_cards.source: American Red Cross First Aid manual

quick_cards.title: Make water safe to drink
steps: Bring clear water to a rolling boil for 1 minute.
Let it cool. Store it in clean, covered containers.
quick_cards.source: CDC, Making Water Safe in an Emergency

quick_cards.title: Keep warm without power
steps: Close off unused rooms and gather in one.
Never run a generator, grill or camp stove indoors.
Wear layers and a hat; keep blankets off the floor.

quick_cards.title: Is food in the fridge still safe?
steps: A closed fridge keeps food cold for about 4 hours.
Throw out meat, dairy and leftovers kept above 40 °F for over 2 hours.
quick_cards.source: USDA, Keeping Food Safe During an Emergency
